avoid_when: A category has hundreds of values (give them numbers instead)

about.example: Region north/south becomes columns north = 1/0 and south = 1/0.
outputs: One 0/1 column for each category value
about.summary_plain: Changes a category, such as region, into one yes/no column for each value. Then models that need numbers can use it.
about.title: Categories to yes/no columns

unseen_levels.description: error, fill (all zeros) or pooled (training level frequencies)

steps.summary: One-hot indicators of categorical variables
steps.summary_plain: Turns categories into yes/no columns

assumptions: The codes are never real values
avoid_when: All numbers are real measurements
data_needs: Columns with placeholder codes
about.example: A temperature of -99 becomes a missing value.
outputs: The same columns with gaps in place of the codes
about.summary_plain: Marks placeholder numbers, such as -99 or 9999, as missing. Some systems use these numbers for 'unknown'.
about.title: Placeholder numbers to missing
use_when: Your source uses codes such as -99 for missing values

above.description: Values strictly above this are missing
above.title: Above

below.description: Values strictly below this are missing
below.title: Below

steps.summary: Turn sentinel codes into missing values

assumptions: You can add spend and sales together. Prices and rates get an average (select this for each column)
When the step needs full periods, it removes an incomplete first or last period
avoid_when: Your data already has one row for each week or month
You cannot add the numbers together, and an average hides the important information
data_needs: A date column with a regular interval
about.example: If the daily TV spend is 100 every day, the week that ends on Sunday gets 700.
about.expert_notes: Group-by on the time coordinate at the target frequency (pandas offset alias). `how` for each variable (sum, mean, last). `full_periods_only` removes partial bins.
outputs: The same columns with one row for each week or month
about.summary_plain: Adds the daily (or hourly) numbers together into one number for each week or month. Each row then covers the same length of time.
about.title: Weekly or monthly totals
use_when: Your data is daily, but you plan and report by week or month
A model needs weekly data

full_periods_only.description: Drop periods that are not fully covered by the source data
full_periods_only.title: Full Periods Only

skipna.description: Ignore missing values (a period with only missing values stays NaN)
skipna.title: Skipna

steps.summary: Aggregate a time dim to a coarser frequency

assumptions: You set the shape and its settings. The model does not learn them from the data
avoid_when: The model learns saturation itself (the Bayesian MMM does this)
data_needs: Media spend or exposure
about.example: With half-saturation at 1000, a spend of 1000 gives half of the maximum effect.
about.expert_notes: Logistic (lam), Hill (slope, half) or Michaelis-Menten curves, applied element by element.
outputs: Media columns on a curved scale
about.summary_plain: Bends spend so that each extra unit of money adds a little less than the unit before. This is what occurs when a channel is saturated.
about.title: Diminishing returns
use_when: You model media with a simple model and you need diminishing returns

by.description: Dim whose levels key per-level parameters
by.title: By

steps.summary: Saturation curve with fixed parameters
steps.summary_plain: Models diminishing returns of extra spend

assumptions: The step can remove empty combinations. It keeps a record of them, so you can put them back
avoid_when: The model can use the grid directly
data_needs: Two or more dimensions to combine
about.example: 3 markets by 4 products become 12 market-product cells.
outputs: One combined dimension
about.summary_plain: Combines two or more dimensions, such as market and product, into one list of cells.
about.title: Combine dimensions
use_when: A model works on a flat list of cells, not on a grid

steps.summary: Stack dims into one
steps.summary_plain: Combines several dimensions into a single list of cells

assumptions: The step learns the average and the spread from the training data only
avoid_when: Zero must keep its meaning (a spend of zero must stay zero)
data_needs: Numeric columns
about.example: If temperatures have an average of 15 and a spread of 5, 20 degrees becomes 1.0.
outputs: The same columns with average 0 and spread 1
about.summary_plain: Moves each series so that its average is zero, and stretches it so that its typical spread is one.
about.title: Centre and scale
use_when: You compare the size of effects across inputs that have different units

fill_mean.description: Mean used for unseen levels with 'fill'
fill_mean.title: Fill Mean

fill_sd.description: SD used for unseen levels with 'fill'
fill_sd.title: Fill Sd

steps.summary: Standardise to zero mean and unit variance over the named dims
steps.summary_plain: Centres each series and scales it to unit spread

assumptions: Missing values or a mask mark the padding cells
avoid_when: All groups have the same number of rows and the model needs a grid
data_needs: A group dimension (customer) and a position dimension (trip number)
about.example: Household 1 with 3 trips and household 2 with 1 trip become 4 rows.
outputs: The same values with one row for each observation and a group index
about.summary_plain: Changes a table where the rows of each group are side by side into one row for each observation. It removes the empty padding.
about.title: One row per observation
use_when: A model works on individual observations, such as shopping trips
Groups have very different numbers of rows

drop_missing.description: Drop rows where every listed variable is missing
drop_missing.title: Drop Missing

mask.description: Boolean padding mask (one of vars); rows where it is False go
mask.title: Mask

vars.description: Every variable on the padded grid

steps.summary: Padded ragged data to long form

assumptions: The gaps have a mark, so the model can ignore them
avoid_when: Your data is already a grid
data_needs: A group column and an order in each group

assumptions: The drift continues at the same rate into the future

power.description: Polynomial power of the scaled trend
power.title: Power

assumptions: The parts of each combined label are known
